plates.side_label: 1819–1820 RUNGE ISOLATION (1.2–1.5 G PER 100 G BEANS) & 1895–1897 FISCHER PURINE RING (C8H10N4O2, SUBLIMATES 235–238 °C)

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked chemical isolation and purine-ring diagram from Friedlieb Ferdinand Runge (1820, Neueste phytochemische Entdeckungen) and Emil Fischer (1895–1897) shows 100 grams of green Coffea arabica beans yielding ~1.2 to 1.5 grams of silky white caffeine crystals (C8H10N4O2, sublimating at 235–238 °C) built around a two-ring purine core with three methyl (CH3) groups.

teach_overlay.label: 100 G GREEN ARABICA BEANS → 1.2–1.5 G WHITE CAFFEINE NEEDLES (C8H10N4O2, 1,3,7-TRIMETHYLXANTHINE)

teach_overlay.scale: every single cup of brewed coffee holds roughly a tenth of a gram of pure white caffeine needles — about the weight of three grains of rice
